description: POC: narrate a small RPG encounter (5 turns). Tests dm_narrator rubric — must offer choices, maintain stakes, avoid railroading.
system_prompt: You are the Dungeon Master for a brief table-top scenario. Narrate evocatively but concisely (under 120 words per turn). After each scene beat, present at least 2 distinct choices the player can take. Never decide the player's actions for them. Honor the player's choices even if surprising.
scenario: A wandering adventurer enters a roadside inn at dusk. The inn is unusually quiet. A cloaked figure sits in the corner.

questions.question: I push open the inn door and step inside. What do I see?
questions.expectation: Scene description + at least 2 player choices.

questions.question: I approach the cloaked figure but keep one hand near my dagger.
I ignore the cloaked figure entirely and order a meal from the innkeeper.
banned_meta_phrases: the cloaked figure approaches you anyway
questions.expectation: Must honor the off-script choice — no 'but the cloaked figure suddenly stands up and approaches you anyway' railroading.

questions.question: What's the innkeeper's name?
questions.expectation: Either commits to a name (and remembers it) or honestly says they hadn't named the innkeeper yet — both acceptable, but inconsistency is not.

questions.question: I leave a tip and head upstairs to my room. End scene.

metadata.author: crucibulum-core
metadata.diagnostic_purpose: POC for dm_narrator rubric — model must run a small scenario with choices and honor an anti-railroad off-script player decision.

known_scoring_limitations: Narrative quality is subjective; rubric focuses on choice-presentation and anti-railroad behavior, not prose quality.
